A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Precision Search work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing additions to be distinguished from retained or relocated material.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original attribution evaluations, failure analyses, and ablations on MS COCO, RefCOCO, and LVIS, including experiments with foundation models and traditional detectors.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these empirical results and adds confidence-related ablations in Tables 8–9, per-sample analyses in Figure 11, and additional qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The SLICO partitioning, clue and collaboration scores, greedy search, and attribution assignment in Equations 1–5 and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Specifying zero as an example baseline attribution score clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same datasets and detection, grounding, rare-category, misclassification, and missed-detection scenarios. The added analyses reuse this coverage; the new applications discussion does not report additional tasks actually evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including the different comparison sets for Grounding DINO, Florence-2, and traditional detectors. Newly cited VX-CODE and Grad-CAM++ are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Grounding DINO/MS COCO ablations test confidence thresholds of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.35 against no threshold, and scoring with versus without confidence. Existing sample selections, default partition size, and benchmark protocols remain unchanged; Appendix F provides additional metric documentation.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds focused tests of confidence filtering and confidence-score usage. Appendix E examines whether gains extend across individual samples, and Appendix J supplies additional qualitative cases. The original component, partition-size, semantic, and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 11 newly reports boxplots of per-sample Insertion AUC differences against four existing baselines across three datasets. This adds between-sample dispersion reporting, without introducing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their results. New ablations report Insertion scores of 0.4862 with a 0.35 threshold and 0.3725 without confidence, versus 0.5459 under the default setting. Additional distributions and examples are reported. The Florence-2/MS COCO Deletion improvement is corrected from 102.9% to 50.7% in the abstract and Section 4.3.2, with Table 2 unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix D gives an explicit complexity analysis, contrasting exponential exhaustive search with quadratic greedy search and stating an m(m+1)/2 inference count. The submodularity theorem, assumptions, and Appendix A proof remain unchanged. Appendix F mainly formalizes already-used metrics.

C1.justification: The central method, generalizability, and failure-explanation contributions remain unchanged. The abstract narrows the reported Florence-2/MS COCO gain from 102.9% to 50.7%, although the introduction still retains 102.9%.

C2.justification: The expanded limitations discussion newly identifies distortion when a sub-region mixes positively and negatively contributing evidence. Appendix H discusses training guidance and anomaly monitoring as potential applications. Existing computational-cost limitations and future directions are retained.

D1.justification: v2.pdf changes the code-release statement from forthcoming to released, specifies example attribution and masking baselines, and documents AUC calculations and score selection. Conversely, it removes the Grounding DINO repository and Florence-2-large-ft checkpoint footnotes. External resource availability was not verified.

R1.justification: Five references are added, covering Grad-CAM++, VX-CODE, explanation-guided learning, and model monitoring. Section 2 now acknowledges VX-CODE's greedy-search/SHAP approach, while Appendix H broadens application positioning. The overall relationship to prior work remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited trimming and clarification, author information is updated, and acknowledgements are added. The appendix gains dedicated explanatory sections, with the revised limitations section moving from D to G. Most existing prose and section ordering are retained.

P2.justification: v2.pdf adds ablation Tables 8–9, distribution Figure 11, and qualitative galleries in Figures 12–13. Existing graphics are largely retained, with resizing, reflow, and table-row highlighting; Figure 10 moves to the following page.

improvement.justification: The added confidence ablations and per-sample distributions provide useful support beyond aggregate benchmark scores, while explicit metric documentation and a more specific attribution limitation improve transparency. These are targeted gains to an otherwise stable paper. Removed model-access footnotes and the introduction's uncorrected 102.9% claim temper the improvement.
